utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. For the second time today I'd like to greet everyone here in this courtroom. I would also like to greet Mr. Prlic, Mr. Praljak, and Mr. Stojic who are here today, and their three colleagues have been taken ill. There is an epidemic of influenza currently going on in Scheveningen, and I'd like to wish them all well, to wish Mr. Petkovic well. They will have all the weekend to get better. We will continue the proceedings with a witness, but I first would like to give the registrar -- we need two IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. OTP has submitted a list of documents to be tendered through Witness DH. The list submitted by OTP shall be given Exhibit number IC 505. Finally, OTP has submitted a response to Defence objections regarding OTP exhibits tendered through Witness Salem Ceranic, and it will shall be given IC number 506. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could just go to private session for a moment, please, on the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, madam. First, I would like to make sure that you can hear me in language that you understand. If that's case, please tell me that you can hear me and understand me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, you are a Prosecution witness. Before asking you to read the solemn declaration, can you give me your first name, last name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Ferida Likic, born on the 8th of April, 1955, in the village of Lankovic [as interpreted], near Olovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have an occupation, madam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm just a housewife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you ever testified before a court of law about the facts that took place -- or the events that took place in your country or is it the first time that you're testifying about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, once in Zenica, but not that much because I'm a sickly woman. I couldn't really take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You testified before the court of Zenica. Do you know the name of the case in which you testified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Against the HVO. Oh, you mean about my testimony in Zenica or the statement I gave in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the court in Zenica. You testified in a trial against whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Against Como Ilijasevic, Dominik Ilijasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me give you few words of explanation. You will have to answer questions put to you by Mr. Scott. You've met him already, of course. Following the questions of Mr. Scott, the Defence that is sitting on your left, and the accused as well, may ask you further questions. The three Judges sitting before you may also put a number of questions to you, but from now on we prefer to wait for both parties to put questions to the witnesses before asking our questions, to allow both parties to develop their arguments through their own questions. If at any time during your testimony you feel unwell, please do not hesitate to tell it us that you want a break, to rest a little bit. That's the way we're going to proceed this afternoon. I'm now going to give the floor to Mr. Scott, who will lead the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Likic.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, just a -- very quickly cover some background material and from -- we'll go into private session -- I'll ask to go into private session in a moment or two, but again for the record, madam, your name is Ferida Likic. You were born on the 8th of April, 1955, Milankovici, a village in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Olovo municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct that you married Mehmed Likic --

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- in 1975 and lived together with him in Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And your husband was a mason by trade?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go into private session for just a couple of questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, just again additional background. In 1993, you and your family lived in the village of Stupni Do in Vares municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The particular part of the village which might be described as a small group of six houses, was there a particular name or term for that particular part of the village that you can tell the Judges?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Perica Do. That's what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in general, this may come up in a number of contexts, but I'm just going to ask you now, madam, was your husband during this time or at any time, but in particular 1993, was your husband ever a member of the Territorial Defence or the ABiH or any military force or organisation?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, madam, that Stupni Do consisted in 1993 of approximately 60 houses, not including stables and barns?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At sometime in the early 1990s had a certain number of houses in the village been occupied by Serbs or Serb families?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Serb families lived there in 10 houses in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And at some point in time in the early 1990s, did the Serb families leave the village?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: The Serbs left the village in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe to the Judges the circumstances in which the Serbs left the village, how that came about and how it happened?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: The Serbs left the village because the HVO came, disarmed them, and then they left in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether there were any Croat families or Croat persons living in the village of Stupni Do in 1993?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was there a woman who lived in the village, a married name, Ana Likic?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Just this one Ana Likic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And she was a Croat and her -- what was her maiden name, please?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Mrljic was her last name, Ana Mrljic, and her married name is Ana Likic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was she married to a Muslim in the village named Alija Likic?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct, madam, that then, as you've described it, all other persons living in Stupni Do as of -- during 1993, except for Ana Likic, were all Muslim?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges whether you recall a time in about June 1993 when a number of Croats arrived in the Vares area from Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Their refugees came. Many of them came to Vares. I don't know the exact figure, but Vares was full of refugees from Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, whether the arrival and presence of the Croats from Kakanj made the local relationships between the Croats and the Muslims better, worse, or did they stay the same?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, they got worse, unfortunately. A worsening was felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just describe to the Judges briefly some of the ways in which that -- some of the ways in which you saw that being carried out, conduct or behaviour that you may have observed or things that were said?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the way it was: I was a housewife. I had my own two cows. I produce dairy products. I went to the marketplace to sell my products every Saturday, and it was obvious that they were taunting our women. They were threatened, our women were, and we felt some fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And madam, just so the record is clear, when you said you went to town, are you talking about the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Vares, yes. That's nearby. It's two kilometres away from my village. Two kilometres and 700 metres, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I want to direct your attention, please, to around the same time that the Croats arrived from Kakanj. Was an ultimatum given to the Muslims in the village of Stupni Do? In June 1993.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges about that?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, we got this ultimatum seven days earlier. I don't remember the exact dates that some unit of ours, a unit of the army, should surrender its weapons. So that's when we got this ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you recall how you came to know of the ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: I remember Husnija Mahmutovic was president of the local commune, and he informed the villagers that we had been presented with an ultimatum. Since my husband was over there at that meeting, he found out that this ultimatum had been presented, and he told us that there was an ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you and your family do anything in response to this ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. From his childhood my husband had a heart problem. He was a disabled person. He had also suffered an accident in the mine. He was in no army, and he was worried about his children, his daughter, and he tried to get them over to Strijezovo to his sister's house. So then all the people moved out of the village because of this ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges approximately, and just as best you can, the approximate percentage or number of the people, the Stupni Do residents, who left the village around that time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: 80 per cent. Perhaps even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, did that include men, women, and children or not?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Elderly people, women, children, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how did these people -- how did the villagers leave the village, by what means?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: They left through the woods, because they wouldn't let us out without some kind of passes, so then we all had to go through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you explain that a bit further? You've made -- mentioned a couple of things. You said you had to have passes, and in order to essentially avoid that requirement, is what I understand you to be saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, would you allow me to clarify a point?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, you have said everybody left the village, and then you gave the example of elderly, women, children. You did not say anything about men of medium age, let's say between 20 and 50, 60. Did they also leave or did they stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The men stayed, and a few of us women, five of us, to tend to the cattle, to milk the cows, things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as these events unfolded, ma'am, can you tell us, did you come to know about a meeting involving Mr. Husnija Mahmutovic and a Croat man from Vares?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, because Husnija lived across the street from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what did you learn about this meeting, and who was involved in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: A gentleman came called Pipe, and he called Husnija Mahmutovic to come and attend a meeting in Vares, and Himzo Likic too. Since we women were afraid, there were only five of us in the village, we were terrified. We didn't let them go, but they said, "It's better for us to go than all of you." So they went to Vares to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, just to be clear, you mentioned I think a few moments ago, Mr. Mahmutovic was the village president; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is that why he was involved in this meeting, as far as you know.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, yes. He communicated with these people, and among the local communes, and I guess that Pipe was the one communicating with him, as far as I know, as far as I managed to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the other member of the village who you named, Himzo Likic, did he hold any particular position or function the village that caused him to be involved in this?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had a position in his own right or whether he was accompanying someone. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do I understand you correctly to say, then, that Mr. Mahmutovic and Mr. Likic then in fact did go down to the town of Vares and meet with the HVO authorities there?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges whether Mr. Mahmutovic and Mr. Likic came back to the village later that afternoon with someone else?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon they returned to the village with Mr. Pejcinovic and some soldiers of theirs from Vares. I don't know whether they were policemen or soldiers. I'm not knowledgeable about this kind of thing. I am a housewife. I didn't even give it any thought. So they came to the village, and they went to Sevko Likic. They sat there for a while, had a meeting. We waited there for them to come out in the street. We were waiting to find out what would happen. They went out. Mr. Pejcinovic asked us, "Why is it so quiet in this village? What's going on?" And we said that we moved out our population, that there were very few of us left, that we were afraid that something would happen to us. And he guaranteed to us, and everybody gave us guarantees. They all persuaded us to get the population back, saying that we would be safe. We were so pleased. We were so happy. We considered this to be the truth, 100 per cent, and within 15 days we returned the entire population to the village, 100 per cent of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, in moving forward from that, can I ask you that later on in the summer, as the summer continued, can you tell us whether any of the Muslim men from Stupni Do were arrested or detained by any local authorities?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. When our people went down to Vares to buy something they would be brought in and then released, and they arrested Mufid Likic in a cafe, then they detained him for about two days, and then he fled or was released, but he came all beaten up, and then we all went to see him. His face was black and blue, swollen. He was beaten in the chest too. So that's what it was like. All sorts of things were going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you remember if anything happened to a man named Rifet Likic during that time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a friend of my brother-in-law. He was a young man of 25 years. He had had four or five surgeries on his legs. He was a disabled person, didn't harm anybody, was a good person, a kind person. They took him to Vares. They interrogated him, wrote something down and later on released him to go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The time when you mentioned a moment ago Mufid Likic being arrested and beaten, can you tell us the approximate -- if you remember the month that that happened in 1993?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, not exactly. July or August, thereabout. At around that time. I don't know the dates. I never thought about the dates. I never even thought that I would get here. I never thought that the truth would be investigated here so that the people in the world would know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: At sometime in September of 1993, was a check-point erected on one of the roads from Vares-Majdan to Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you ever pass through that check-point?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every Saturday and on my regular trips to the doctor I would pass by.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you heard that, ma'am. They would like you to -- if you can possibly move a little bit closer to the microphone, so -- if that's possible, if you can still do that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher, could you help the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, you indicated that every Saturday on your regular trips to the doctor you would pass through this check-point. Do you know who manned or who were the people that were -- that operated or were present at this check-point?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, those were the soldiers from Vares, soldiers of the HVO who were residents of Vares. I didn't know any of them personally so I couldn't give you any names. I didn't know those who were younger than me. I was just a farmer, and I was busy trying to make a living and taking care of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have any understanding of why this check-point was erected and operated between Vares and Stupni Do at that time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know until my daughter was stopped. They took from her the food that she had purchased for our household.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Let me now move forward to October of 1993, if we can, and can you tell the Judges what you know about the arrest of six men from the village in October 1993?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I didn't know where the men were. I didn't know what was happening to them. I didn't know how they were arrested. One of these men, Himzo Likic, is my husband's brother. They were arrested, and I don't know how my husband learned about this. He just came and said that they had been arrested. He said he was worried about what was going on. He didn't know why our people were being arrested. They wanted to go across that road that was still open to us. Later on that road was obstructed as well and we didn't pass through. This is how I learned of their arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you can recall, can you name the persons who -- the men who were arrested at this time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Esef Likic, Resad Likic, Mufid Likic, Jakub Likic, Himzo Likic, and Ahmed Likic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were these all Muslim men from the village of Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: All Muslims and relatives, cousins, relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct, madam, that your husband went and visited these men or saw that these men were being detained in Vares?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was still working in the company, in the mining company. Since he was a disabled person, he worked in a -- in a bathroom as the leader of that team. He went to visit them, and upon his return I could see that he was disappointed. He was crying. He was worried. We knew that we would not be able to leave the village after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me come back to that in just a moment, but did you learn either from your husband or otherwise around this time where these six men were held? Where were they detained in Vares?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: My husband told me that next to the municipal building, in the building of the secondary school where they kept them in the gym, I guess. Later on they were transferred to Vares-Majdan before the attack on Stupni Do. In the Second World War there was a prison there in that building, and this is where they transferred them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask -- can I ask you now to go back to the statement you made just a moment ago. You said that this concerned you because this meant that, "We would not be able to leave the village after that." What do you mean by that, and why did you feel that way after this had happened?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Because that was the only road open to us. It was a hidden road through the forest, and then they discovered this road and they blocked it. And after that one couldn't leave any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the record is clear, madam, when you say "They discovered it," and, "They blocked it," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Those were the HVO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, while we're still on the question of these men who were detained or men who were detained in Vares town, we're jumping ahead of ourselves a bit but I'd like to take this now if we can. Can you tell the Judges whether you ever learned that some of the men who were detained in Vares were -- during the attack on Stupni Do taken to place where they could see what was happening or at least part of what was happening in Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those who could walk were taken away, and then some members of the Likic family were disabled, couldn't walk. Those who were from Majdan-Vares, a friend of my husband told me this upon my return to Vares when he came to visit me, and he asked me whether they had tortured my husband, and I said, no, they killed him. And he said, "Well, he was a fortunate person, because they took us to Perun to see the village on fire. They beat us, and those who were unable to leave, unable to walk out, they remained in prison."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said, madam, that they took these people or some of these men to a place called Perun, P-e-r-u-n. Can you tell the Judges what that place was and where that was in relationship to the village of Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: It's towards the village above the school in Majdan-Vares, facing our village. That's a mountain called Perun, and they took them there so that they could watch it and so that they could torture them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what these men could see, as you understand it from, from this location at Perun on the 23rd of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: They could see raging fire, smoke. That's all they could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in talking -- you talked to one of the men who was actually taken to that location on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And before I move on to another topic, can you just -- did this man ever indicate to you why -- what was his understanding of why they had been taken to this location to see -- to observe Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: They took them because these Muslim men who were in town were not members of any army, so they kept saying to them, "Look what happened to your army, to Alija's army. Why don't you join our army." They mistreated them. To force them to join the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, going back to the arrest of the six men from village that you talked about a few moments ago, can you just indicate, and perhaps you did but how far -- how many days prior to the attack on Stupni Do did that happen, approximately?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately eight days prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what was the impact of the arrest of these six men on the people who lived -- the Muslims living in the village?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, it was significant. We were afraid. People, even elderly ones, joined village guards. They guarded around houses to make sure that nothing would happen, and unfortunately things did happen to us. Everybody was anxious. Everybody was on alert. We were expecting something terrible, and something terrible did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, you just mentioned a village guard. I want to ask a few questions about that. Was a village guard, something called a village guard, organised in Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Village guard, that's all it was, to my knowledge. Now, whether there was anything else there, I don't know. I didn't go and see. I was a housewife, and all I knew was what my husband told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you know approximately when this village guard was organised, if you know?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: When these people were arrested, all of this was organised and then they just kept watch to make sure that things wouldn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, approximately how many men comprised or made up this guard?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: About 20, thereabouts. I don't know the exact number, but around 20 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges whether these were all men who lived in Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you have any information that you can assist us with, madam, do you know how this village guard was armed?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. They said that some of them had hunting rifle, and I don't know anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, now let me direct your attention, please, to the night of the 22nd of October, 1993. Did anyone to your knowledge leave the village on the night of 22nd October?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ana Likic left the village. Her brother came to fetch her, and he took Ana and her husband, Alija. Many Ana went to her sister-in-law, Serifa, telling her to watch out and take care of themselves, and then she left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, madam that the woman you just mentioned is the same woman you identified some moments ago earlier this afternoon as, "this was the only Croat who lived in Stupni Do"?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm sure that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you know who came and took her out of the village on the night of the 22nd of October?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Her brother came, I don't know his name, and he took her from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And before we move on to the next morning, can you tell the Judges to your knowledge did anyone else leave the village of Stupni Do around this time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Prior to that, I don't know which date it was, only a woman left with a child, her grandchild, who was four to five years old. How they left the village, I don't know. Whether they received passes or not, I don't know. I know that they used to be in the village, and then they were the only ones who left it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So is it correct, then, madam that apart from Ana Likic and this one woman and her grandchild that as of the night of the 22nd of October, as far as you know, all the other members of the village were in the village?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges whether this information that Ana Likic had left the village, did that become known in the village that evening?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: It became known because she told her sister-in-law, Serifa, that she was leaving, and then she in turn informed the residents. I was at home because my hamlet was further away from the village. My husband came and he told me. We had a barn in the village and our cow was there, and my husband had come from the village and he asked me what I was doing. I was cooking dinner. He said, "Get your bags ready. Get everything ready." And I asked him what happened, and he said Ana Likic had left. Her brother came to fetch her. This was when panic started spreading in all houses in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges a bit more about that, why? I mean, why did the departure of this one woman and her husband from the village have such an impact on the people living in the village?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, because she was the only Croat. And she was a wonderful woman, a beautiful woman. I can't say a word against her. Her brother came to take her away so that she would come to no harm, and based on that we concluded that something would happen and, unfortunately, did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Apart from that, this event of Ana Likic leaving the village, can you tell the Judges was there any other warning or notice that the HVO would attack the village on the 23rd of October?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm taking you now to the morning of the 23rd of October. Can you tell the Judges what happened that morning?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. On the 23rd of October, at 8.00, a shell landed in the village. Since I didn't know what was a shell, I hadn't had occasion to hear it explode until that time. I was having breakfast with my children in the house. My husband was sleeping, having returned at 7.00 from his duty in village guard. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: As I open the door, I could hear a lot of shooting. I didn't know what was going on. I went back inside the house. My children were crying. My husband had gotten up. He was awake. He was pale and terrified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An order, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... know what to do. We looked at each other. Then I went again. I saw a boy. His name was Audin. He was screaming. He was terrified. Audin Likic was his name. It was dum-dum ammunition, and it was exploding so noisily that we thought we were all about to be killed. And then he came inside and he asked me what to do with his cows. I said, "Forget about your cows. Get inside the house," and he came in the house. We started looking for a shelter inside the house. I was trying to calm down the children. I felt also sorry for my husband. He had never served as a soldier, and I felt bad about the fact that he wasn't able to take charge of all of us, but that's how it was. We came inside the bathroom. Everybody was in panic, crying. I was calming down the children, trying to talk to them, and I was afraid myself. I can't even tell you this coherently. And then at one point I went towards a window because this house was on an elevation and one could see the village, and as I approached the window I saw that there were no more windowpanes and all the glass was broken, and I came back to my family members. I told them that the village was on fire. I didn't know what was going on, who was setting the village on fire, and what was happening in the village. My husband wanted to go out, but I preferred for myself to go out because I didn't want anything to happen to him. However, he went out to see Amir Likic. He lived next door to us. And we wanted to see what we should be doing. He spoke to Amir and his mother Rasida. She had a grandson called Kabir and they made a decision to go to the shelter but I said we should wait a little bit. I don't know how long we remained there. It's impossible to described this to you. I don't think that even a movie would be able to depict it to you realistically. It was that bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me take you back for a moment, please, before you continue. You said when you looked out the window at one point you could see the village burning. Could you identify the houses of any particular villagers, friends or neighbours or family, particular houses that were on fire at that time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised the house of Nezir Beganovic that was on fire, Serif Likic's house, Halid Likic's house, Hafo Likic's house. There were some barns on fire. Everything was engulfed by fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: To go back a moment, you said a moment ago that there was discussion about going to a shelter. What was this shelter, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, we had a shelter dug out close to the forest. It was something that we called shelter, and it was a kind of a trench, dugout. But since there was a clearing between us and the shelter, we were unable to get to the shelter. So we decided to go to the house of Husnija Mahmutovic which was across from our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Approximately how far was Mr. Mahmutovic's house from your house?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: About 20 metres, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, please, the names of the persons who moved from your house around this time to Mr. Mahmutovic's house?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. From my house it was myself, my husband, my daughter, my son, and Likic Audin. From Amir's house -- actually, it's the same house. It was split in half between us. It was Amir Likic, Kabir Likic, and Rasida Likic, nicknamed Sida, and we set out towards Husnija's house. We were running across, across the road. Amir ran across, as did my husband, Nedzad, and then Nedzad fell. I screamed. Nedzad got up and said, "Mum, don't be afraid. I'm fine." As I ran across, I saw that Adisa and Sida were missing. Prior to me Audin had run across. I screamed at them saying, "Run across. Just run," because it was a clearing and they were able to see us clearly and to aim at us, to hit us. And this is how we reached the shelter at Husnija Mahmutovic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you arrived at Mr. Mahmutovic's house, did you find there were other people who were already there? And who were they?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I found there Muamera Mahmutovic, Husnija's wife, her two children Fuad and Mahir, his mother Fatima, his brother Edin, Rifet Likic, Ramiza Likic. There was also a woman from Foca, Halima Kovac, and her sons, Emir and Samir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And could you tell the Judges, please, approximately how long did you remain at the Mahmutovic house?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, not exactly. I don't know exactly. Sometimes it seemed like quite a long time. Sometimes it seemed like only a brief period of time. Half an hour, an hour. I'm unable to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And continue on. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: After that Husnija Mahmutovic came, and he said that they had already entered the village, the HVO army. My husband and Amir went out to see what was going on and came back quickly inside the shelter. I asked him what's going on, and he said, "We need to flee," because they had entered the village, "and I don't know what's going to happen to us." I was so sure that nothing whatsoever would happen to us. And while I was talking to my husband, Amir Likic, Kabir, and Ramiza Likic ran out. They fled to the forest without us noticing that. Then we moved towards the door, and then all of a sudden there was such tremendous noise in Husnija's house. People running. We could hear their shoes banging in the house. They started yelling, cursing at us, cursing our balijas, mothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you said you could hear boots on the floor?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: In the basement, in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And you say you could hear boots on the floor?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Of course. Of course, you could hear it from upstairs. There was banging. There was cursing. We could hear all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: We returned to the shelter because we were surrounded. We couldn't go anywhere. We returned to the shelter. We didn't have any small children there either. The youngest child was four or five years old. We had to tell him to keep quiet. Everybody was terrified. We were all quiet in this shelter, and all of a sudden we heard a woman's voice shouting, "Get out. They'll kill you. They know about you." That was Suada Likic who they had brought with her. Now, did she tell us herself or did she have to tell us, I don't know. I don't hold it against her, because whatever they said to her she had to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Then we went out. Two soldiers came to the door. They said "Get out or otherwise we're going to throw grenades and kill you." We went out. We surrendered, all of us. We all went outside. As we were getting out outside they started separating us, the men, women, and children, but all of that was nearby, a metre or two, men on one side, women on the other side. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to go into private session for a few moments, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll move briefly into private session, Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, we're back in open session and I want to go back. You said that when you came out of the shelter there were HVO soldiers around. I think -- I think it's -- we've lost the page on the transcript now, but approximately how many soldiers do you recall seeing around the house when you came out?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: A lot. I saw between 20 and 40 of them. Lots of them, that's for sure. And also on the road leading to Vares-Majdan, those who did not quite walk up to us. I don't know. I don't know. It was a war. There was shooting. I could not count all of these people, and I cannot know all these details. I didn't have enough time. I didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you -- as best you can remember, ma'am, can you tell the Judges how these HVO soldiers were dressed?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: The HVO soldiers wore camouflage clothing, some of them, and others in black clothing, and we first thought that they weren't even HVO. We thought they were Serbs. Was it maybe the Serb army that came from up there? What was this? What is this black? So that's how they were equipped. They had these white ribbons on their arms. I don't know what that help.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where on their arms did they have these ribbons, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Here. They were tied up here on their arms. I don't know why and what for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you see any other symbols or badges on these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, on this camouflage uniform you could see -- well, I mean, who'd look? You would see that it's HVO insignia. On the black ones we couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you see any other symbols or markings on their uniforms or what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. No. No. No. I just saw that they had this paint on, and some of them had black ribbons on their heads. Some of them had crosses around their necks. Some of them had wooden crosses, others had glittering crosses and then they had the letter U. I don't know what that meant. They looked like people who work on a railway except they had black caps, sort of like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where about them, on their bodies or on their clothing, did they have this letter U?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: On the cap.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, did you recognise any of these HVO soldiers as soldiers from Vares?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't. I didn't really know many people, especially not young-ish people. I was a housewife, you know. And I went to the marketplace once a week selling my dairy products. I didn't know many people. I knew perhaps older people or women who came to buy my cheese and cream and other dairy products. Perhaps it's easier to explain it that way. But my husband recognised one of them and called out his name. "What are you doing to us? We're neighbours. Why don't you say that we're not in any army?" And the other one hit him immediately and said, "There's no neighbours here. It's only people from elsewhere." I didn't really know anyone. I didn't recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges whether -- you could see any other parts of the village or houses on fire at that point after you'd been taken out of the shelter and you were with this group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw my house was on fire and my barn was on fire. Everything was on fire. The village was on fire as far as you could see. Everything was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you said --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Madam, you said a few minutes ago that when you were taken out of the house, when you came out of the -- Husnija Mahmutovic's house that there was some effort to separate the men and the women; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us more about what happened in that regard?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: I can. They separated the men from the women. The men were on one side, and we women and children were on the other side near Edin Mahmutovic's small summer house. So it was only a metre or two away. I really don't know what to say, how people were lined up. Everybody was so afraid and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry. Were the group of you standing on the road that ran between your house and Mr. Mahmutovic's house?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. That's when we got out of the shelter. That question belongs there. So we were standing towards Mahmutovic Fatima's house and in the middle there was this little summer house of Edin Mahmutovic. That's where we were standing, right in front of Husnija's house when we got oust shelter that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you were all then standing, with the men on one side and the women on the other side, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, what happened. It was so fast. They were swearing at us, saying, "Hand over your money. Hand over your jewellery. Hand over everything," and we did. We gave them everything we had, jewellery, money. Then he walked up to Rifet Likic. He asked him for money and he, poor thing, didn't have any money. He was young, a young man, and there was a war, and he said, "I haven't got any money." And then this man hit him on the right side. Since he didn't exactly cut him, he was facing us, all the men were facing us, he sort of held on this way with his hands, but there was blood seeping through his fingers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am -- ma'am, I'm sorry. Sorry to interrupt you, but we may have missed something or it may have been something you said a few minutes ago. You said just how that he hit him, but now you said that there was -- you saw blood coming from his neck, the way you described it and the way you showed it. What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Oh, but of course. Of course. He hit him way up here across the neck. It looked as if his throat had been slit. There was blood seeping through his fingers. The children didn't dare look. The children closed their eyes, whereas we had to see it. We had to see what was going on. And Rifet bent over, and the soldier hit him, and he fell and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry. Either -- it may be my question or it may be translation or it may be just a misunderstanding, I'm sorry to interrupt you. When you say he hit him in the throat, in the neck, did he had hit him with his hand or was he holding anything in his hand when he hit him?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. Knife. He was holding a knife. He used a knife, and he slit his throat, but obviously he didn't quite slit it because otherwise he couldn't bend over, but he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Rifet, as he was holding on this way, there was blood seeping through his fingers, and then this one hit him with a rifle on the back and he fell, and that's the side where we were. When you go from Husnija's to Fatima's house there was this slope and he fell. And he shot at him had, and again Rifet tried to get up. Now, the strength he had, I really don't know. Then he got closer to him and then, you know, a few times in the head. I don't know how many times. It was so fast. It was like a burst of gunfire, and he walked up to my husband only, and my husband --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry. Let my interrupt you again. When you said that this soldier shot at Rifet, how far away was he? How far was the end of his barrel of the gun, of the rifle, from Mr. Likic's body when the shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, say half a metre, not more than that. All of that is so close.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you said at one point Rifet was still trying to get up?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then again he was shot in the head, and then there was no more Rifet. He was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What happened after that? Are you okay --

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: They went up to my husband --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- ma'am?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: -- my husband. They were asking for money. He got his wallet out, gave them what he had. I don't know myself how much money he had in his wallet. He held his wallet in his left hand and he gave them the money with his right hand. He ordered Edin and my husband to lie on their stomachs, and they were close to me like this -- or, rather, on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How far was your husband from you when he was lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, like this. Like a metre and a half or two. And the rifle was nearby, and then he shot him between the shoulder blades, and that's how he killed Mahmutovic too. And then they were taking all of this jewellery. And they killed the two of them. I mean, I really don't know. I mean, I really cannot tell you about all of these things that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, I know this is difficult for you, but was your husband killed immediately or did the two of you have a chance to see each other before he died?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: When he laid down, as they were to kill him, he turned to the left and he looked at me. And I looked at him, and I saw them kill him. His eyes were begging for help, but there was no help.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we should take the break now at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll take a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I was told via the Victims and Witnesses Section that the witness is concerned as to the length of the examination, so for psychological reasons I will ask all parties to try and reduce as much as they can the time they need for questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, you've told us so far --

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You've told us so he far about the killing of Mr. Rifet Likic and also your husband. Was there a boy named Mahir who was part of the group that was gathered at the location you've described to us this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did anything happen to him during this time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: One of the soldiers there -- I keep saying one of the soldiers, you know, but one of the soldiers wanted to slash his throat, and he threw him to the ground and took the knife out to slit his throat, and then when he saw his mother leaning over, he saw that she had earrings in her ears, and he started cursing and he said, "Look at her. She did not hand over her earrings." So he let the boy go. And I approached the mother, took the earrings, and gave them to the soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the name of this woman, please?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Muamer Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And why did you take her earrings and give them to the soldier?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, once I saw them at the ready with the knife, I was worried that they would cut off her ears or something. So I jumped in to take her earrings off. I don't even know where I got that strength. I guess I was totally unconscious of my own power at that moment, but I did it to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was the -- I think you mentioned earlier when I ask you who was at the shelter, who came out, that sort of thing, but was a woman named Sida Likic part of this group?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was. She stood next to me in the line. She was first, and then I was next, and then Nedzad was next to me. He was 14, but he wasn't tall. I mean, he appeared to be younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened to Sida Likic at this time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Sida Likic asked that they not harm the children. They said, "Why? Are the children bothering you?" And then this man kicked Sida, and he bent her over a stump that was used to cut -- to chop wood, and then he fired in her shoulders, between her shoulders. Sida was all bent over. She was crying. She was saying, "My legs are hurting," but it was all to no avail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the transcript, just before we continue on, you said that Sida Likic asked that they not harm the children, and they said, "Why? Are the children bothering you?" Is that something that they the soldiers said, "Why? Are the children bothering you?", or is that something that the Sida Likic said?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. Sida Likic said that. "Why are you harming the children? Why are the children bothering you?" She begged them, "Do not harm us," but they killed her nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at -- there's a bundle of documents there in front of you or to your -- on your right side under the tissues.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Could you please help me with the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please. Would you please go to Exhibit 9886. It may be helpful, usher, if you could maybe put that on the -- we have an extra copy we can put on the ELMO. Ma'am, while that's being done, let me just go back and again just clarify something while we're in the process of getting the document together. You said that they had Sida bent over a stump that was used to cut -- to chop wood, and then he fired in her shoulders. It may be obvious, but when you say he fired in her shoulders, what do you mean? What happened? Ma'am?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, he fired at her, killed her. That's obvious. She was lifeless. She was all bent over as they threw her on the ground. That's how she remained lying there. One of my legs was under her, and I had to pull my leg out so that they wouldn't see it. I was afraid. I was afraid just like anybody is afraid of dying. That's how I pulled out my leg, and she remained lying there. I could see her muscles contracting and then they stopped, and I could see her coat moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, can I ask you to look at this diagram, please, and I know that the writing -- all or most of the writing on the document is in English, but that's not what I'm asking you about. If you can look at the diagram, please, enough to orient yourself to -- to it, and then I'm going to ask you, please, if you could point out your house on this map. And I guess I should say, first of all, is this a diagram or map of the village of Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you find your house on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is where my house is, right here, and then this is the house of Husnija Mahmutovic. This is the shelter. This is the summer house of Edin Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, let me stop you for a moment.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: This is the house of Fatima Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The Judges can't see what you're pointing out. Can ask you to use the map that is on this machine to the right, and the usher will help you, because that way everyone in the courtroom will be able to see what you're pointing to. So again can you please -- looking at that diagram, can you show us where your house was located.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: This is my house, right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I ask you, please, to -- if a marker can be provided to the witness. Can you circle your house, please, draw a circle around your house and put number 1?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where -- then you talked about going across -- travelling a distance of approximately 20 metres to the house of Husnija Mahmutovic. Can you show us Mr. Mahmutovic's house?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the house of Husnija Mahmutovic. This is where we came down, crossed the road, and came to his house here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you please to draw a circle around that and mark that number 2.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, at the time that your husband and these others were killed, can you show us the location -- that location on the map?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: We were right next to this summer house, and they were right next to us here in front of Husnija's house. This is all next to each other. Two or three metres away, from this house to Husnija's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you to just mark that location that you've just been pointing to with a number 3.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. In a few minutes, madam, we're going to talk about -- you may have just mentioned it now, but while we have the map in front of us could you also show us again, if you have already, these -- what you call the summer house? Where was that located?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Number 3 is the small house of Edin Mahmutovic, and then this is the house of Fatima, his mother, the one that we haven't marked yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you to do exactly that. Can you please mark Fatima's house and put a circle around that and please mark that with a number 4.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions about this diagram, but if the -- if the Judges had a question now, perhaps it would be the appropriate time. No. Okay. Thank you very much. We are finished with that drawing then. If we can get an IC number for that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will become Exhibit IC 507.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, can you please sign this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Somewhere here. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the time when you were in this -- the area that you've been describing now for some minutes this afternoon, did you at any time see a soldier that you knew or came to know as Como?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. We heard them call out the name, but as I was giving this statement for The Hague Tribunal, I didn't dare give any names because my brother is a lawyer and he said that that could harm my children. He said I should watch out because you never know what people might do behind your back. So I never wanted to give those names. I called and called out the name of Como, Ljubo. Ljubo is a Serbian name. And it seemed to me as though they wanted to create confusion, to mislead us with those names. And then the one called Como was angry that they were calling out names. That's how I knew those names, but I didn't recognise anyone's appearance. Some of them were disguised. They had painted faces and all that. I didn't recognise any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you said a moment ago that the one called Como became angry that people were speaking out loud and calling out names, what did he do or say when he became angry about that?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: He yelled at them and he cursed them, but the words that he used are bad, in my opinion. He cursed God, and he told them, "Why are you using names?" He used bad language, and then they stopped calling out names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you at this point before we move on to another topic, during that day on the 23rd of October, at this point and at any point while you were able to look out at the village or moving about the village yourself, did you see any women in the village carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, had we had weapons, some people would have defended themselves. Where could we have obtained weapons? How could have women obtained weapons? If I had a weapon I wouldn't allow anyone to approach me in the shelter. Things that happened to me would not have happened to me. I didn't know anyone who had any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me -- just for purposes -- so the record is clear, ma'am, we have your general answer, but let me just be very specific, if you can answer my question. Did you see any women in Stupni Do on 23rd of October, 1993, who were carrying or firing a weapon?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned several times that when -- for instance, when you were gathered there together, the group of you that you've told us about this afternoon, that money and jewellery was taken away from you. Can you tell the Judges whether any property was taken from houses?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. The soldiers took out things of value. I saw one soldier taking out of Husnija Mahmutovic's house new sneakers. He tied them around his neck, and they were just hanging there. Then one of them took a backpack saying, "I will take this to my wife." And he threw the other bag of ours into fire so that everything perished in fire and we had nothing, absolutely nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you see any other houses being put on fire after your husband was killed?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: I saw the village and everything around it on fire. Everything was on fire. We thought that nobody else was alive, that we were the only ones who were there and were captured. We didn't know what was going to happen to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you identify the Judges -- up to that point in time, and when I say that point in time, ma'am, I'm talking about when you were still there in that area around where your husband and the others had been killed, were there any houses in that area up to that point had not been put on fire?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. They were on fire. Just Husnija's and Fatima's house were not on fire yet. My house had already been on fire. Likic's house was -- my large barn was on fire too. I saw it burning. And then just the houses immediately around us were not on fire yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was anything -- did you hear the soldiers, the HVO soldiers, say anything about those houses?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, no. Just at one point in time a soldier cursed us, insulted us in all kinds of ways. Then he said, "What are you going to do? There's no Alija to defend you." And we really didn't need anything at that point because we didn't know whether we would survive. It was terrible. Those were terrible shocks, traumas. I have scars from them to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did anything happen then to Husnija's house and Fatima's house?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. A soldier yelled out, "Why aren't they setting houses on fire?" And then he fired into Husnija's house. He fired from some kind of a weapon. I'm totally ignorant when it comes to weapons. And then all of a sudden the roof came in and the house was on fire. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can please go into private session for a few moments, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, for a few minutes let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'd like to direct your attention now to -- we've mentioned the several times already today the summer house. Can you tell the Judges then what happened in connection -- anything involving the summer house, and if you could just basically take us through what happened.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. When they killed Rasida Likic, a soldier started firing around my feet, trying to taunt me. I was totally powerless. I guess I was in shock, but I didn't beg him. I didn't cry. The one with Motorola said, "No more killing. She deserves a bullet, but she's not going to get one." Then the other one asked, "What are we going to do with them?" The commander ordered that even children in -- in cradles had to be killed. The houses were on fire. Fatima's and Husnija's houses were already on fire. I was afraid they would throw us into the fire alive. My two children were with me. One of them said, "We are going to set them on fire in this small house," and he forced us into the house. This was a young man. He looked terribly. His eyes were all bloody. He came inside this house. Edin Mahmutovic lived there. He was a bit mentally disturbed. It's not that he was harmful to anyone. He took his eau de cologne and drank it. I could see right away that this was unimaginable. How can somebody drink that? How could somebody do that? He threw things around the house. He forced us into a corner, made us sit there, the 12 of us remaining there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a moment, I'm sorry. You just said 12 people. Who was gone -- who was put into the summer house at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I think it would be safer and we could move more quickly if we could just go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again was at some point the summer house put on fire?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: We did not see how they put the summer house on fire. We stayed there quiet, terrified. The soldier who went out locked the door. We heard the key as he locked the door. We were so afraid. Then he wanted to see whether he could open the door. He kicked the door. As I was standing there, I couldn't sit down, the children were on this bed or whatever. I don't know what word to use for it. I was standing. This door was low, and I saw the HVO soldiers moving about putting corpses into the fire, but I did not see who it was that they were carrying. I just saw them carrying them. I stayed there, sitting there for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give the Judges any more information about in which house, if you can, the soldiers, the HVO soldiers were putting bodies?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Fatima Mahmutovic's house. That's where they carried the corpses. They set us on fire and left. My -- my son was sitting by the window in the small summer house, and he looked through the window and said, "Mum, you ought to see this, all these soldiers moving through the village." And I looked through the window and I saw there was no one. I just saw this one man running. I did not see masses of people, and I was wondering whether my child had gone crazy by then. So we were waiting, and all of a sudden the windows started breaking because it was so hot. The fire was getting close to us, and I was suggesting that we should get out. It's better for them to kill us with a bullet than to burn. And everybody was crying and begging me, "Mum, don't open the door. We have water here. We will try to put the fire out." But nevertheless, I decided, and Suada Likic saw this little axe on this little piece of furniture that we have in the village, and I got up and I asked Fatima Mahmutovic just to hit the lock so that it gets a bit shaky and then I would open the door with a little axe. And then I said to them, "Run to the woods. Whoever they kill, they will kill. Whoever they wound, they will wound, but just run to the forest." I went out to see where the corps were. I guess I was in a state of shock. I didn't see anything. I didn't hear them running next to me, nothing. As I turned around I walked into this little house. Fatima was standing by herself next to the doorstep, and I said, "Why didn't you leave?" And she said, "I can't," because her son had been kill. She said, "I cannot run. I cannot escape. I cannot go." And I said, "I can," as I was so afraid. I ran towards my children to see where they were. But before that I just looked a bit to see whether I could get the corpses out. No, it was not possible. All three houses were on fire, Husnija's and Edin's and Fatima's. You could not even stand close to that. It wasn't like fire -- well, what kind of fire was it? Was it because of the furniture or the clothing. You could feel all these smells, all sorts of things. That's the way --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you -- sorry. Let me ask you before we have to move forward, you said you looked a bit to "see whether I could get the corpses out." Could you see any of the corpses that were in the house, any of the burning houses at that time and, if so, if you could identify them, then please do. Sorry to ask you that, but if you can.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see because the fire was getting out of the door. I couldn't see. I couldn't figure it out. I just saw that they carried them in there, and I just tried to look through the fire to see whether I could save someone from that fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And after you escaped from the summer house and after you had tried to look around into what you've just described, look into these burning houses, what did you and the others do after that?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, I went to the woods. I found the children, the women who had fled down towards the forest. Amir and Ramiza, I found them too. They were with us before. They were in the forest as well. They asked me where Fatima was, and I told them she stayed behind, I don't know, in the little house up there, and I followed the children. I said to Amir, "Your mother was killed. Don't wait. There is nothing to wait for any more. We have to go into the forest. We have to seek shelter." And that's how we left. The first night in the forest we were on our own. We didn't know if anybody from the village had survive. We didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long were you in the forest before you either came to a check-point or someone collected you, or how long were you in the forest, approximately?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: We were in that forest until the morning of the 25th, Monday. The people who survived sort of gathered there. I don't know how they survived. In the morning, after dawn, we all gathered there, and then we spent another night there. And then on Monday, the 25th, we decided to surrender to the HVO yet again since we had little babies. They didn't have any food. It wasn't even possible to breast feed them because the women were in trouble out of fear or whatever. Also, there were some women who could or could not get their period. They didn't have any sanitary pads. And we all started smelling, and we couldn't stand the sight of one another any longer. And then we decided to surrender, to go further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before you go further with your story, could you tell the Judges by Monday the 25th of October, approximately how many people from the village had gathered together by that time in the forest?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, not say anything for sure, but there were about a hundred of us. Up to 100. I don't know whether it was exactly 100, but it was women, children, old men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm going to -- at the moment I'm going to show you some additional exhibits, and if we have time I will come back to try to finish very quickly the rest of your story, if you will, but before we do that can I ask you if, in that bundle that is in front you, can you look at 6116. And Exhibit 6116, madam, and for the courtroom, is a collection of nine photographs. Can you just tell the Judges briefly -- in looking at these photographs yesterday, can you confirm that these were all photographs of the village of Stupni Do after the attack on the 23rd of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Stupni Do. These are photographs of Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you -- each of the pictures has a number on it you will see, and again because of the time I'm going to ask if you can please find -- I think the first photograph in the bundle is 0035-7812. Perhaps if in e-court we could go to that if possible. 7812.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell -- in looking at that, can you tell the Judges if you recognise or know anyone's -- that to be anyone's house or one of those remaining structures, whatever's left to be the house of anyone that you knew at the time?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: It is hard to recognise all of this, but these are houses of Stupni Do. This is Arif Likic and Salih Likic's house. And then up here, well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, if you continue through the bundle and if you can please find the photograph that is marked 0035-7832.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to direct your attention to a house that's roughly -- not exactly but roughly in the middle of the photograph, and at least according to the light it looks as if -- whether it does or not, it looks as if it has kind of a blue wall. Do you recognise that house and who had lived there?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: The one in the middle of the photograph is Salim Likic's house. Then down here is Mujo Likic's; then Alija Likic; and then Rozovic, Dragica, her barn, and I don't know, all these ruins put together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, because of time unless the Chamber wants to I'm not going to mark the individual houses, but again of course if the Chamber wants to do that we can, but obviously it will take time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you to go to exhibit -- photograph 0035-8464.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll just ask the usher -- we're going to be going through all the remaining documents, and it may be easier for you to just assist her there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can find 35 -- 0035-8464. Can you identify that house, the house shown in that photograph, please?
