utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Fatima Mahmutovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if we can go, please -- I'm sorry, Your Honour, but if we can go into private session for just one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Usher, can you assist the witness, please, by directing her attention to Exhibit 6314. Madam, Exhibit 6314 is a bundle of autopsy reports, and can I please ask you if you can find toward the end of the bundle in the Bosnian language on page 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The English pages are numbered, page 41, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you have that -- and if you look for the one that has the name Mehmed Likic. Do you have that? Do you see it, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is this an autopsy of person who -- identified here as your husband, Mehmed Likic?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In looking at the report, ma'am, can I ask you is it correct that it says that the body of this person was "completely carbonised"?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At the time when you saw your husband being killed, as you described for us early this afternoon, was his -- it may be stating the obvious, but can you tell the Judges, was his body at any time around that time on fire?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: No. No, I couldn't get to the body. Had I seen him, I would have saved him even though he was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I ask you, a few pages back, if you move a few pages back toward the front of that bundle can you please find a similar document concerning Refet Likic -- Rifet Likic, on page 37 of the English translation?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Rifet Likic is Mehmed's brother's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did also -- looking at the text or the content of the report, do you see that it also indicates that, this "body carbonised"?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were together. They were burned together. The bodies were carbonised and taken for a post-mortem, but I have never believed that they could tell who was who, but they were buried one next to the other so that the wounds and scars would be less painful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, Exhibits 8662, 8660, 8663, and 8658 are respectively the death certificates of Mehmed Likic, Rifet Likic, Rasida Likic, and Edin Mahmutovic. I would hope that there would not be any dispute about that, and I wouldn't take the time with the witness to show her those documents if we don't need to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections and I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- that's on behalf of all the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One final -- yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have seen all these documents yesterday, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One last document, then, and then we will conclude the -- at least my questions will be concluded. If you can 8382 [Realtime transcript read in error "8232"], please. Can you just tell the Judges briefly what that document is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be a mistake on the transcript. I think it should be -- it should read 8382.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Your Honour. If I misspoke, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what is that document, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Well, this is, I guess, a document concerning my house in Stupni Do, that it was destroyed, set on fire, built in 1978, and the size of the house, 8 X 4, and so on. The basement consists of a basement. The house was built in 1978. The house is 8 X 8, and it consists of a basement and -- and a ground floor. What's this, this 4, 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just ask you in the interests of time, is this the record of an inspection that was done in 1994 just to confirm the property lost by you and your family on the 23rd of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just to conclude, then, madam, and again we don't have the time to go through this in all detail, you said a few moments ago that because of the poor conditions that the group were in, there were babies, people were cold, there was no food, did you turn yourself in to an HVO check-point?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We turned ourselves in at a check-point of Pajtov Han, towards the village of Strijezovo and towards Breza. That's where we went. We got out of the forest. We decided to surrender. My daughter didn't want to. She stayed on, and then she stayed with a friend, and her friend told her what it was that had happen. She didn't want to go without her, and she stayed with my daughter, and her father stayed, too, and we surrendered. As we appeared, as we got out of the forest we saw their APCs and their check-point and there was this camouflage APC facing Vares and it was painted all camouflage and shooting started straight away. They started shooting at us straight away. They were shooting in order to scare us but they didn't wound any one of us. We just walked up to the check-point, and when we got to the check-point, we just found three soldiers there at the check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. What I'm going to have you ask you now, please, is just -- later after this -- approaching the check-point and having seen these three soldiers, did there come a time when UNPROFOR vehicles, the UN protection force, in other words, that the UNPROFOR vehicles came to this check-point and collected you?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR vehicles did not arrive immediately. I don't know how much time went by and what happened, but we were there for a long time, and we didn't know what it was that was moving from down there because they said that nothing or no one could move up or down. And then they put us into this prefabricated building. Who wanted to go into it could go in, and who didn't want to could stay in front on the road. And we were supposed to get onto -- into these vehicles, and then there was this curve, and we said we'd better sit on this road and let them run us over. There's nothing else for us to do. The women went out with the children. There were wounded men, women, little girls. We were all there. And then all of a sudden two sort of little trucks, or whatever, of UNPROFOR came. It wasn't an APC. And it stopped, and as they stopped a young-ish man got out. I don't know whether he was a Swede or whatever. He got out, and he said, "Are you the women from Stupni Do?" And the women started crying, screaming. Children were crying. And they -- and he said, "Take it easy. Take it easy. I don't understand much Bosnian, but I can help you." Things got a bit more quiet. He offered the women milk and to the children, too, gave them some food as well, and even now in my years I hear the children saying, "Give us bread. Give us bread." He walked up to this soldier. They called Cicko. Some of them knew him from before. I didn't know him until that day. And he said, I mean this Swede said that Cicko should stay away from us, and the HVO soldiers too. They didn't want to. He was very fair. He ordered the soldiers to do what they could with their weapons, and then he started negotiating with Cicko. And he said, "I want to take these women and children from Stupni Do. Can I talk to Duznovic, and where am I going to find Duznovic?" Cicko said, "Duznovic has nothing to do with this. You will have to negotiate with Ivica Rajic and Ivica Gavran." I remember that, and I said to my son Nedzad, "Remember those two names, son, if I die." I was so exhausted I couldn't stand on my two feet, and I couldn't walk any more, but I knew that this Ivica Rajic -- I mean, that this last name did not exist in Vares, and I was wondering what was this, and what did this man hold against us in our village? Why did he come to our village and do what he did to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ma'am, let me just stop with this: Were you then taken by UNPROFOR later that day to Breza?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Those who could not move around at all went to Breza, the wounded, women who had young children. I wanted to get onto the truck, too, but there was no more room left. Another group of HVO soldiers came up, and I guess this one soldier knew me, and he walked up to me and he congratulated me on going to my own people. And I don't know what people I was with before then. I fell. He lifted me up, and he said, "Fuck you, woman, what's wrong with you now? You're going out to be free." And I said my daughter's in the forest. And he said, "Stay behind. You and I will go to the forest to find her." I guess this man was one of our people from Vares who wanted to help me, but I couldn't move. I couldn't walk. I couldn't return. And I said, "Please, if my daughter comes up, please don't do anything to her. Let her leave. Let her get out." That's the promise he made. And we set out. I was taken by two Swedish men who helped me walk. Each took one side of my arm. And there was a column between the trucks. And I couldn't speak to them, but they took me to about one kilometre away from their check-point. Someone from the forest shouted out, "Ferida, Ferida, come over here. Your countryman." And when they asked me what they were saying I didn't dare say. I didn't say. I suppose it was the BH army. And the person who knew how to speak came by and told them to come up closer and they did come up closer, closer to us. They approached us, two men, and they took me over on a stretcher and took me towards Strijezovo. And Nedzad my son went towards Breza and my daughter remained in the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, ma'am, and I'm afraid we'll have to leave it at this: Then were you reunited in the next couple of days with your son and your daughter in Breza?

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I waited for two days. I was staying with my sister-in-law. Some people said, "She's left the forest." Others said she hadn't. I wasn't sure what had happened. I wasn't conscious of anything. And then a cousin of my husband's came by and said, "Your son's with me. You needn't worry. He's in Breza." And then I set out on foot towards Breza, and so did go of my other neighbours, women. And two days later I was at Strijezovo, and we went across some fields to Dabravine, the village of Dabravine, and suddenly a car appeared, a red car. I expected (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An order, please. Please proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The man got out. I didn't know him, but the woman who was with me, it was a cousin of hers, and they kissed by way of greeting and she cried. And he said, "Why are you crying? Where are your children?" And she said, "Here." She had two little sons. And she said, "Why are you crying? How do you suppose this other woman feels?" And I started crying even more. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's try to conclude, please, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ms. Likic, I want to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and giving this very important testimony. I know it's been very difficult for you. I'm sorry for that. But I think that everyone in the courtroom appreciates your courage in telling your story. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: FERIDA LIKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, too. Thank you for having me come here. I haven't come here to -- because of anyone or because I like The Hague. I just want the truth to be known, a truth that's been waited for 14 years. That's why I have come, to help my dead buried in the ground, to know that I still live for them and speak for them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mrs. Likic, I would like to ask you a very simple question just because there might be a confusion. The woman who had been standing next to you and was shot in the back when she was over a stump, you said she was called Sida. At another moment you called her Rasida, and there is also a document, "Rasida." Am I right in supposing that Sida is short for Rasida and it's the same person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Hvala ljepo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. She was nicknamed Sida but her real name was Rasida. Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, madam. Can we continue before the break? It may be that the Defence might have very few questions. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have no questions for this witness but we do wish to thank her for coming here to The Hague to give her evidence. Thank you very much, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We also have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Murphy. Ms. Pinter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, the Defence of General Praljak does have some questions, three questions, but may we go into private session for that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Private session for three questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, madam, we have no questions for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. Thank you for understanding me. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, we have no questions either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no question. Any redirect, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ever so briefly, Your Honour. I just -- this issue of the name, I don't think we need to be in private session for the name of this individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we might have to do that because we went into private session the first time. So back -- back to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in open session, I want to thank you on behalf of my fellow Judges. Thank you for coming to testify in The Hague on events that are particularly painful for you. We are ever so thankful to you. Our very best wishes for your return to your country.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you too. Thank you to the Defence counsel and the Prosecution for understanding me. You all understood me nicely, and I'm happy that I was able to go through all this. Thank you. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Usher is going to take you out the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, just before we conclude, with regard to next week we have a schedule, don't we? As far as I know there is no problem, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No. Excuse me, Your Honour. No. I don't think any of these individuals will have protective measures. I hate -- I would hate to make a mistake, but, no. The individuals next week are all scheduled. As you know Mr. van der Weijden is returning for cross-examination on Monday, and I believe it's followed by Mr. Burger and also Mr. Draper who are both UNPROFOR officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, listen, today the hearing stands adjourned. We shall reconvene next week on Monday at 2.15. Thank you.
